library(knitr)

# Set to TRUE only when you want to (re)write the PDFs in ../figures/pdfs/
save_pdfs <- FALSE

# Figure filenames start with the Rmd's name, e.g. alpha-glucosidase-2026-08-17_Alina-boxplot-1

pdf_to_folder <- function(file, width, height, ...) {

                 width = width, height = height, ...)
}

  fig.path = paste0("../figures/knitted_mds/", fig_prefix, "-"),

)

```{r libraries, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
 
# Folder holding the plate-reader exports (edit if they live elsewhere)
data_dir    <- "../data"
results_dir <- "../results"
```
 
# Overview
 
Sigma-Aldrich alpha-Glucosidase Activity Assay Kit (MAK123), read at 405 nm
on the older plate reader at USU. That reader couldn't run a kinetic
protocol, so the plate was read twice by hand: once at the start (run 1) and
once at 20 min (run 2). Each run is a separate .xls file.
 
Five single larvae per group:
 
- **Wild R**: wild larvae from the resistant field samples (SLC), live
- **Yellow**: susceptible wild/colony larvae (yellow), live
- **Green**: resistant colony, live
- **SLCMAD**: susceptible colony, stored in 50% glycerol / 50% PBS at room
  temperature for about 3 days (from 08/14) before the assay
 
**Activity.** From the kit:
 
$$\text{Activity (U/L)} = \frac{A405_{final} - A405_{initial}}{A405_{calibrator} - A405_{water}} \times 250$$
 
- *initial* = run 1; *final* = run 2 (20 min)
- calibrator and water = their run 2 reads
- If A405_final > 1.0, the kit says to dilute with water and repeat. Set
  `dilution` in the plate map for any re-run well and the result is
  multiplied back up.
 
One unit hydrolyzes 1.0 µmole substrate per minute at pH 7.0.
 
# Plate map
 
From Alina's plate map. All other wells were empty.
 
```{r plate-map}
file_initial <- file.path(data_dir, "8-17-26 assay run 1.xls")   # t = 0
file_final   <- file.path(data_dir, "8-17-26 assay run 2.xls")   # t = 20 min
run_label    <- "2026-08-17"
 
water_well <- "A1"   # H2O control
cal_well   <- "A2"   # calibrator
 
# Ordered from most susceptible to most resistant, wild resistant last
colony_order <- c("Yellow", "SLCMAD", "Green", "Wild R")
 
plate_map <- data.frame(
  well     = c(paste0("B", 1:5), paste0("C", 1:5), paste0("D", 1:5), paste0("E", 1:5)),
  colony   = rep(c("Wild R", "Yellow", "Green", "SLCMAD"), each = 5),
  dilution = 1
)
```
 
# Colors
 
Presentation palette and plot labels, matching 10/01, the master summary and
the Lsph probit figures (higher contrast; Yellow is a mustard gold). The wild
resistant samples aren't one of the colonies, so they are drawn in near-black
grey. Labels give each colony's RR50 vs. SLCMAD at 24 h.
 
```{r colors}
colony_colors <- c(Yellow   = "#B8860B",
                   SLCMAD   = "#005A9C",
                   Green    = "#007A55",
                   "Wild R" = "grey20")
 
colony_labels <- c(Yellow   = "Yellow\nColony\n(RR50=0.251)",
                   SLCMAD   = "SLCMAD\nColony\n(RR50=1)",
                   Green    = "Green\nColony\n(RR50=9,090)",
                   "Wild R" = "Wild SLC\n(survivors)")
```
 
# Data
 
Each .xls holds one 8 x 12 plate of A405 values. The plate block is found by
its row label "A", so a different number of header rows doesn't matter.
 
```{r read-data}
read_plate <- function(file) {
  x <- suppressMessages(read_excel(file, sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE,
                                   col_types = "text"))
  first <- which(x[[1]] == "A")[1]
  block <- as.data.frame(x[first:(first + 7), 1:13])
  absorbance <- sapply(block[, 2:13], as.numeric)       # 8 rows x 12 columns
  data.frame(well = paste0(rep(block[[1]], 12), rep(1:12, each = 8)),
             abs  = as.vector(absorbance))
}
 
initial <- read_plate(file_initial)
final   <- read_plate(file_final)
stopifnot(identical(initial$well, final$well))
 
plates <- data.frame(well = initial$well,
                     A405_initial = initial$abs, A405_final = final$abs)
```
 
# Activity
 
```{r activity}
water_20 <- plates$A405_final[plates$well == water_well]
cal_20   <- plates$A405_final[plates$well == cal_well]
denom    <- cal_20 - water_20
cat(sprintf("Calibrator (%s) at 20 min = %.4f\nWater (%s) at 20 min = %.4f\n",
            cal_well, cal_20, water_well, water_20))
 
agc <- merge(plate_map, plates, by = "well", sort = FALSE)
agc$activity_U_L <- (agc$A405_final - agc$A405_initial) / denom * 250 * agc$dilution
agc$over_1       <- agc$A405_final > 1.0
agc$colony       <- factor(agc$colony, levels = colony_order)
agc <- agc[order(agc$colony, agc$well), ]
 
if (any(agc$over_1))
  warning("A405_final > 1.0 in wells: ", paste(agc$well[agc$over_1], collapse = ", "),
          " -- kit says dilute and repeat.")
 
write.csv(agc, file.path(results_dir, paste0("agc_activity_", run_label, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)
kable(agc, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
 
## Summary by group
 
```{r summary}
agc_summary <- data.frame(
  colony   = colony_order,
  n        = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$colony, length)),
  mean_U_L = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$colony, mean)),
  sd_U_L   = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$colony, sd))
)
agc_summary$cv_pct <- 100 * agc_summary$sd_U_L / agc_summary$mean_U_L
 
write.csv(agc_summary, file.path(results_dir, paste0("agc_summary_", run_label, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)
kable(agc_summary, digits = 1)
```
 
# Boxplot
 
Ordered from most susceptible to most resistant (as in the probit panel), with
the wild resistant samples last. Points are individual larvae.
 
```{r boxplot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5.5}
cols <- colony_colors[colony_order]
 
par(mar = c(5.5, 4.8, 3, 1))
boxplot(activity_U_L ~ colony, data = agc,
        col    = adjustcolor(cols, alpha.f = 0.35),
        border = cols,
        lwd = 1.5, outline = FALSE, las = 1, xaxt = "n",
        ylim = c(0, max(agc$activity_U_L) * 1.1),
        xlab = "",
        ylab = expression(alpha*"-glucosidase activity (U/L)"),
        main = expression(alpha*"-glucosidase activity by colony (08/17/2026)"))
set.seed(1)
points(jitter(as.numeric(agc$colony), amount = 0.12), agc$activity_U_L,
       pch = 16, cex = 1.2,
       col = adjustcolor(colony_colors[as.character(agc$colony)], alpha.f = 0.8))
axis(1, at = seq_along(colony_order), labels = FALSE)
# mtext() draws every multi-line label (axis() can drop ones that come close)
mtext(colony_labels[colony_order], side = 1, at = seq_along(colony_order),
      line = 0.8, padj = 1, cex = 0.8)
mtext("Single larvae, n = 5 per group; SLCMAD stored 3 days in glycerol/PBS",
      side = 3, line = 0.2, cex = 0.8, col = "grey40")
```
 
# QC: reader stability
 
There are no kinetic reads, so instead: the empty wells and the water and
calibrator wells should read the same in both runs if the reader was stable
between them.
 
```{r qc-stability}
empty <- plates[!plates$well %in% c(plate_map$well, water_well, cal_well), ]
qc <- data.frame(
  wells   = c("Empty wells (mean)", "Water (A1)", "Calibrator (A2)"),
  run_1   = c(mean(empty$A405_initial), plates$A405_initial[plates$well == water_well],
              plates$A405_initial[plates$well == cal_well]),
  run_2   = c(mean(empty$A405_final),   water_20, cal_20)
)
qc$change <- qc$run_2 - qc$run_1
kable(qc, digits = 4)
cat(sprintf("Largest change in any empty well between runs: %.3f\n",
            max(abs(empty$A405_final - empty$A405_initial))))
```
 
# Notes
 
*Summary for Alina and the lab, written 10/22/2026.*
 
- **Two manual reads.** Activity comes from just two reads (start and 20 min)
  taken by hand on the older USU reader, so the 20-min interval and the
  temperature were not logged. Alina has noted that this reader has trouble
  regulating temperature. Values from this plate may not be directly
  comparable with the 09/11 and 10/01 plates, which were read on the
  Multiskan SkyHigh with logged 20-min kinetic runs.
- **No check on linearity.** With only two reads per well, there is no way to
  see whether a well's signal rose steadily or jumped, as the kinetic QC
  plots can on later plates.
- **SLCMAD was stored, the others were live.** SLCMAD larvae spent about 3
  days in 50% glycerol / 50% PBS at room temperature; the other three groups
  were assayed live. Storage is confounded with colony here.
- **Pattern.** SLCMAD again reads clearly higher than the other groups, which
  are similar to one another (see the summary table). On 10/01 the stored
  wild resistant larvae read as high as SLCMAD, while the live wild resistant
  larvae here do not; whether those are the same collection, and whether
  storage raises activity, is worth checking.
- Small n: 5 single larvae per group, so group differences should be treated
  as preliminary.
